partners.mechanism_chain: PRKAR1A (HGNC:9408) —DISRUPTS→ cAMP-PKA signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); cAMP-PKA signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —DECREASES→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167984); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167984) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0011556); PRKAR1A (HGNC:9408) —LEADS_TO→ Pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (MONDO:0012509). Loss-of-function mutations in PRKAR1A (encoding the regulatory subunit of Protein Kinase A) disrupt the normal regulation of the cAMP-PKA signaling pathway. In the context of PPNAD1, this leads to constitutive activation of PKA, resulting in adrenal hyperplasia and nodule formation. In BCC susceptibility, the disrupted PKA signaling indirectly affects the Hedgehog pathway, which is crucial for epidermal development and differentiation, leading to uncontrolled proliferation and tumor formation.

falsification.text: If pathogenic variants in PRKAR1A are found to be exclusively associated with either basal cell carcinoma or primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease, and not shared between them, this hypothesis would be falsified. falsification.gnomad_variant: Discovery of common (>1%) benign variants in PRKAR1A in gnomAD populations that are also pathogenic for either disease.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. basal cell nevus syndrome 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787, Reactome:R-HSA-5632681, Reactome:R-HSA-5632684, Reactome:R-HSA-5635838, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9585) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-2025170); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-2025170) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002650); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-2025170) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell nevus syndrome (HP:0002650). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 disrupt the normal regulation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, leading to both basal cell carcinoma and basal cell nevus syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PTCH1 that consistently lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in both disease contexts, or the absence of any PTCH1 variants in individuals with these phenotypes. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway is a viable therapeutic strategy for both basal cell carcinoma and basal cell nevus syndrome.

---

#### 2. Curry-Jones syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787, Reactome:R-HSA-5632684, Reactome:R-HSA-5635838, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9541) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457); SMO (HGNC:10740) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002670); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP457) —LEADS_TO→ Curry-Jones syndrome phenotype (MONDO:0011134). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 (a negative regulator of Hedgehog signaling) and SMO (a positive mediator of Hedgehog signaling) lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway. This aberrant pathway activation is a shared mechanism contributing to the development of basal cell carcinoma and the complex phenotype of Curry-Jones syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PTCH1 or SMO in patients with basal cell carcinoma susceptibility 1 or Curry-Jones syndrome lead to opposite functional effects (e.g., gain-of-function in one and loss-of-function in the other) or that the Hedgehog signaling pathway is not implicated in either disease. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.01) in PTCH1 or SMO in the general population that is not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** The shared reliance on the Hedgehog signaling pathway presents a therapeutic opportunity. Inhibitors of this pathway, such as vismodegib, are already used to treat basal cell carcinoma, suggesting potential for similar targeted therapies for Curry-Jones syndrome, provided the specific clinical manifestations can be addressed by modulating this pathway.

**Proposed mechanism:** SMO (HGNC:10747) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8886690); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8886690) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0011556); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8886690) —LEADS_TO→ Holoprosencephaly 7 (MONDO:0012562). Gain-of-function mutations in SMO lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which is implicated in the pathogenesis of both basal cell carcinoma and holoprosencephaly 7.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a common pathogenic variant in SMO that is consistently associated with only one of the two conditions, or the absence of any SMO variants in affected individuals of either disease. _(variant: rs117716076)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway, particularly SMO, is a therapeutic strategy for basal cell carcinoma, and understanding its role in holoprosencephaly could inform developmental interventions.

#### 4. congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.681)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787, Reactome:R-HSA-5632684, Reactome:R-HSA-5635838, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9548) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP47); SMO (HGNC:10674) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP47); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP47) —LEADS_TO→ basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0011556); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP47) —LEADS_TO→ congenital hypothalamic hamartoma (MONDO:0009436). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 or SMO lead to dysregulation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which in turn contributes to the development of basal cell carcinoma and congenital hypothalamic hamartoma.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PTCH1 or SMO in patients with basal cell carcinoma do not lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog pathway, or that patients with congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome do not harbor mutations in PTCH1 or SMO. _(variant: rs373790648)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway with drugs like vismodegib has shown efficacy in treating basal cell carcinoma, suggesting potential therapeutic avenues for related developmental disorders.

#### 5. Carney complex, type 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.414)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9572) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP475); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP475) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002670); PRKAR1A (HGNC:9305) —DECREASES→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP475); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP:WP475) —LEADS_TO→ Carney complex (HP:0005773). Loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 disrupt the normal inhibitory regulation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, leading to its constitutive activation and the development of basal cell carcinoma. In Carney complex type 1, loss-of-function mutations in PRKAR1A lead to decreased PKA activity, which can indirectly result in altered regulation of the Hedgehog pathway, contributing to the complex's phenotype.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in PTCH1 are found to be exclusively gain-of-function or if PRKAR1A mutations do not show any discernible impact on the Hedgehog signaling pathway in relevant cellular models, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: None specified, as the causal variants are typically rare and private to affected families.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the Hedgehog signaling pathway in both basal cell carcinoma and Carney complex could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate this pathway for the treatment of both conditions. For example, Hedgehog pathway inhibitors are already used for basal cell carcinoma and might be explored for Carney complex.

#### 6. pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease, primary, 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.411)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** PRKAR1A (HGNC:9408) —DISRUPTS→ cAMP-PKA signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); cAMP-PKA signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —DECREASES→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167984); Hedgehog signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-167984) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0011556); PRKAR1A (HGNC:9408) —LEADS_TO→ Pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (MONDO:0012509). Loss-of-function mutations in PRKAR1A (encoding the regulatory subunit of Protein Kinase A) disrupt the normal regulation of the cAMP-PKA signaling pathway. In the context of PPNAD1, this leads to constitutive activation of PKA, resulting in adrenal hyperplasia and nodule formation. In BCC susceptibility, the disrupted PKA signaling indirectly affects the Hedgehog pathway, which is crucial for epidermal development and differentiation, leading to uncontrolled proliferation and tumor formation.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in PRKAR1A are found to be exclusively associated with either basal cell carcinoma or primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease, and not shared between them, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if distinct signaling pathways are definitively shown to be responsible for each disease, independent of PKA signaling, the link would be invalidated. _(variant: Discovery of common (>1%) benign variants in PRKAR1A in gnomAD populations that are also pathogenic for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PRKAR1A and the cAMP-PKA pathway in these distinct diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies. For example, drugs modulating PKA activity or downstream effectors of the Hedgehog pathway could potentially be beneficial for both conditions.

#### 7. complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.357)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gain-of-function variant in PTCH1/SMO —DISRUPTS→ PTCH1 (HGNC:9575); Gain-of-function variant in PTCH1/SMO —DISRUPTS→ SMO (HGNC:10679); PTCH1 (HGNC:9575) —DECREASES→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (GO:0007224); SMO (HGNC:10679) —INCREASES→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (GO:0007224); Hedgehog signaling pathway (GO:0007224) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (MONDO:0011556); Loss-of-function variant in PTCH1/SMO —DISRUPTS→ PTCH1 (HGNC:9575); Loss-of-function variant in PTCH1/SMO —DISRUPTS→ SMO (HGNC:10679); Hedgehog signaling pathway (GO:0007224) —LEADS_TO→ Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 7 (MONDO:0012399). Gain-of-function mutations in PTCH1 or SMO lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, promoting basal cell carcinoma. Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in PTCH1 or SMO disrupt normal neuronal development and migration by altering Hedgehog signaling, resulting in complex cortical dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the specific PTCH1 or SMO variants implicated in basal cell carcinoma do not affect Hedgehog pathway activity, or that the variants causing cortical dysplasia have no impact on this pathway. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in PTCH1 or SMO that are strongly associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Hedgehog signaling pathway is a validated therapeutic strategy for basal cell carcinoma. Understanding its role in cortical development could inform novel therapeutic approaches for brain malformations.

#### 8. cardioacrofacial dysplasia 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.356)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTCH1 (HGNC:9572) —DISRUPTS→ SHH signaling pathway (WP:WP476); SHH signaling pathway (WP:WP476) —LEADS_TO→ Basal cell carcinoma (HP:0002670); RASA1 (HGNC:9787) —DISRUPTS→ SHH signaling pathway (WP:WP476); SHH signaling pathway (WP:WP476) —LEADS_TO→ Cardioacrofacial dysplasia (HP:0012357). Gain-of-function mutations in PTCH1 (or SMO) lead to constitutive activation of the SHH signaling pathway, resulting in basal cell carcinoma. Loss-of-function mutations in RASA1 disrupt negative regulation of the SHH pathway, contributing to cardioacrofacial dysplasia 2. Both diseases converge on the SHH signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in PTCH1, SMO, or RASA1 in patients with these respective diseases, or identification of entirely distinct molecular pathways driving each condition. _(variant: rs373004305)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the divergent effects of mutations within the SHH pathway in these two distinct diseases could inform targeted therapeutic strategies, such as pathway inhibitors for BCC or modulators for CAFSD.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the dual role of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, particularly PTCH1, in both cancer predisposition and developmental disorders could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both conditions, potentially with different modulating agents depending on the specific functional consequence (gain vs. loss of function).
